svg.title: MCPhantom kill chain - deprecated MCP servers installed by AI coding agents
svg.desc: Single-lane chain of six stages: a developer asks an AI agent for an integration, the agent picks a deprecated archived MCP server from training data, installs it with npx without a manifest or CVE, the server persists as a trusted Node process, a prompt injection reaches the agent, and server-puppeteer lets the agent run arbitrary commands. Critical stages are the package choice and the command execution. Detection anchors are the npx command line, MCP client config files and shell children of Node.
svg.text: MCPhantom: deprecated MCP servers installed by AI coding agents
Vendor: Glow Labs (2026-11-02) · Date: 2026-11-04 · Cluster: none (exposure pattern) · Day 134
DEVELOPER ENDPOINT + AI AGENT HARNESS
Developer asks the agent for an integration [T1204]
User asks for 'a GitHub MCP' or similar; in 98% of reviewed sessions the AGENT chooses the package
Seen in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Claude Cowork and Claude chat (Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI)
trigger: natural-language request, no package name from the user
Agent picks a deprecated package from training data [T1195.001]
Anthropic archived 13 of 20 reference servers; deprecated packages vanish from npm search
In one session npm said 'This package is deprecated' and the agent installed anyway
@modelcontextprotocol/server-github|postgres|slack|puppeteer|gitlab|...
Install via npx, no manifest, no CVE [T1195.001]
npx still installs deprecated packages with only a warning (17.3M downloads since 2025-07-10)
SCA has no manifest; EDR sees a trusted Node process fetching a public npm package
generic: npx -y <package> in mcpServers config (.mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json)
MCP server persists and runs as a trusted Node process [T1059]
Server definition stays in the MCP client config and runs with the developer's privileges
Software inventory does not register the app
hunt: config files + node.exe command lines naming deprecated servers
Prompt injection reaches the agent [T1059]
Attacker-controlled content (for example a page the agent browses) instructs the agent
Glow reports no exploitation in the wild; no CVE or GHSA id exists
precondition: agent reads untrusted content with server-puppeteer enabled
Arbitrary command execution via server-puppeteer [T1059]
Agent starts any process instead of the browser; the web-browsing approval covers it
Archived May 2025, maintainers state no fix will come; payload and versions not published
detect: shell or download tool as child of node running server-puppeteer
Detection anchors
Sigma 01-03, KQL k1-k3, YARA (2 rules), Suricata sids 9920001-9920003, PEAK H1-H3. All low confidence: no technical IOC published.
Break points: package choice (managed MCP allowlist, deprecation check) and the permission that covers process start.
